title: Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka
summary: The Mauryan emperor Ashoka had fourteen Major Rock Edicts, public statements of his moral and administrative policies, issued in one body in 258–257 BCE per one reference source. Copies were cut into rock across his realm; the Shahbazgarhi set in the Vale of Peshawar is in Kharosthi script.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO gives 258-257 for the issue of the fourteen Major Rock Edicts in one body and 260 for the first Rock Edicts; UNESCO says the Shahbazgarhi edicts date to the middle of the third century BC. Dating of Ashoka's reign varies between sources (c. 268-232 BCE; r. c. 272-235 BC).

as_recorded.value: In 258-257, he issued in one body the fourteen Major Rock Edicts
Dating to middle of the third century BC

where.modern_name: Shahbazgarhi rock edicts, Mardan District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan (one of several rock-edict sites across the subcontinent)
where.historical_name: Shahbazgarhi, Vale of Peshawar (Gandhara), within Ashoka's Mauryan realm

importance.justification: Public inscriptions announcing a ruler's moral and administrative policies, called indispensable for understanding ancient Indian history by the University of Washington.

reviewer_note: The 258–257 date rests on a single reference source (EBSCO); others give c. 260 BCE for first edicts. The UNESCO tentative-list entry prints the coordinates as "34°12’ E 72’9’ N", with the letters apparently swapped; read here as 34°12′ N, 72°9′ E. The edicts stand at many sites, so the Shahbazgarhi pin is a representative site only.
